verdict: Essex grew revenue 4.1% to $493 million and core FFO edged up to $4.00 a share, while GAAP net income fell to $98 million because last year's quarter included big gains on property sales.

segments.name: Rental income
segments.note: Rent from about 63,000 apartment homes, mostly on the West Coast.

segments.name: Other property revenue
segments.note: Parking, fees and other income from residents.

segments.name: Management & other fees
segments.note: Fees for managing properties owned with partners.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of buildings over their lives — a large non-cash charge for a landlord.

opex.name: Corporate property management
opex.note: Central teams that oversee the apartment portfolio.

opex.name: Impairment, net of gain on sales
opex.note: A $10.7M impairment loss, minus the $6.8M gain on selling real estate this quarter.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $65M, partly offset by $9M of equity income from co-investments and about $2M of swap, interest and other income, plus a $0.5M tax benefit on technology co-investments — a net $53M cost.

follow100.label: Property operating costs & real estate taxes

follow100Note: As a REIT, Essex pays no federal income tax on earnings it distributes to shareholders, so there is no tax slice this quarter.

takeaways.title: Same-property growth
takeaways.text: Revenue from apartments Essex owned in both periods rose 3.0%, led by Northern California at +5.4%; financial occupancy was 96.3%.

takeaways.title: Core FFO per share
takeaways.text: Core funds from operations — the REIT cash-earnings measure — rose 0.8% to $4.00 a share, a cent above the guidance midpoint; the full-year Core FFO midpoint was raised to $16.16.

takeaways.title: GAAP profit fell on comparisons
takeaways.text: Net income available to common shareholders dropped to $98M from $165M mainly because Q3 2025 included $62M of gains on real estate sales, versus $7M this quarter.

oneTimers: Essex sold three apartment communities in the quarter for a combined $111.9M pro-rata price and booked a $6.8M gain on sales, versus $62.3M of gains a year ago.
Expenses include a $10.7M impairment loss (none a year ago).
Essex agreed a $19.25M tenant settlement that also cancels $8.7M of claimed move-out balances, as disclosed with the quarter's results.
footerNote: Essex is an apartment REIT and pays no federal income tax at the REIT level, so the tax line is $0. The impairment line is shown net of the $6.8M gain on real estate sales so operating profit matches the reported earnings from operations. Net income of $104M is the consolidated total; $98M was available to common stockholders. Figures are from the Form 10-Q, reported in $ thousands and rounded here to the nearest $M; depreciation is shown $1M below its rounded value so the rounded chart balances exactly.
